disease_label_per_paper: Mixed connective tissue disease presenting with recurrent epistaxis, myositis, ILD, mild pulmonary hypertension, and renal-crisis-like hypertension
presentation_summary: 35-year-old woman with no past medical history presented with recurrent epistaxis for three months plus fatigue, proximal muscle weakness, appetite/weight loss, GERD symptoms, painful finger cyanosis, migraines, and episodic blurry vision.
Exam showed telangiectasia around the lips, systolic murmur, tight dorsal hand skin, generalized 4/5 weakness, and healing herpes zoster rash; blood pressure was 183/133.

Workup showed hemolytic anemia with elevated LDH and positive Coombs, hypocomplementemia, elevated BNP and troponin, proteinuria, hyperproteinemia, elevated liver tests, and mildly elevated CK; exact values for most of these were not reported.

Serology showed ANA 1:1280, positive anti-Ro/SSA, antiphospholipid antibodies, PL-7 antibodies, and strongly positive Smith/RNP IgG 122 units; dsDNA, anticentromere, Scl-70, and RNA polymerase III were negative.

HRCT showed bilateral lower-lobe interlobular septal thickening, reticulation, and mild ground-glass opacities; PFT showed restriction with reduced DLCO; exercise right-heart catheterization showed mild pulmonary hypertension with mean PA pressure 22 mmHg and normal wedge pressure.

quality_warnings: The paper states most lab abnormalities qualitatively; no numeric values were invented.
Smith/RNP positivity is structured as anti-RNP activity, while the file preserves the paper's caveat that highly specific U1-RNP testing was not performed.
